summary: Temporary elevation approval links show valid window but fail to grant role for non-US timezones
description:
Issue summary: Several internal users reported that temporary elevation approval emails indicate a valid approval window (e.g., 'Approve until 14:30 PDT') but when they click the approval link within the shown window the web UI returns an 'Approval link expired' or grants no roles. Impact: Affected engineers cannot get temporary permissions for runbooks and on-call tasks; leads to delayed incident response and manual intervention by SRE. Scope: Reports primarily from employees in EMEA/APAC timezones, intermittent for US users. Initial hypothesis: time formatting or parsing mismatch between the email template and the RBAC validation service.

Observed behavior:
- Email shows a localized expiration time (human-readable, no timezone offset)
- Clicking the approval link within the visible window returns a page saying the token is expired or the elevation did not apply
- Support audit logs show the approval webhook reached RBAC service but validation failed with a time-check error in a subset of attempts

Expected behavior:
- Approval link should successfully grant the requested role for the duration shown in the email if clicked within that window

Workaround:
- Support can manually grant the role via internal admin tool (rbac-console) after verifying identity
- Temporarily extend approval TTLs on the approval-service (manual config) for affected users until a fix is deployed

Next steps:
- SRE/Eng to reproduce with test accounts across timezones, gather logs and timestamps, and push a targeted fix to parsing/templating logic.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Request temporary elevation via console for an internal tool (e.g., runbook-access) while logged in from a non-US timezone (or simulate via account locale).
2) Receive approval email; observe the human-readable 'Approve until' time in the message (no explicit ISO offset).
3) Click approval link within that window.
4) Observe the approval UI returns 'Approval link expired' or the role is not applied in the console.
5) Check rbac-service logs for the approval webhook and note the timestamp comparison error.
logs:
[2026-03-11T18:22:07Z] approval-service: received approval callback token=abc123 user=michael.t@redwood.com locale=GMT+1
[2026-03-11T18:22:07Z] rbac-service: validate_token token=abc123 issued_at=2026-03-11T17:22:07Z expiry=2026-03-11T18:52:07Z server_time=2026-03-11T18:22:08Z
[2026-03-11T18:22:07Z] rbac-service: validation_result=failed reason="parsed_expiry_missing_tz"
[2026-03-11T18:22:08Z] auth-proxy: returned 400 "Approval link expired" to client

Note: logs show expiry value in template lacks timezone/offset and our parser treats naive timestamps as local-server-time (us-east) causing validation to fail for users outside that zone.
investigation_notes:
Timeline: First reports 2026-03-09. Reproduced in staging by setting browser locale to Europe/Berlin and using an approval flow test user. Findings: The email template is using server-side formatting via Go 'time.Format' with layout that outputs e.g. 'Mar 11 14:30' (no offset). The approval-service signs tokens that embed an expiry as RFC3339 without offset in some code paths due to a legacy util function (time.UTC() vs. time.Local()). RBAC validation code expects RFC3339 with offset and falls back to parsing as server local time, so an EMEA timestamp parsed as server-local (us-east) appears expired when compared in UTC. Reproducible pattern: users whose local timezone is ahead of server time were affected most. Additional contributing factor: email client shows localized time (JS in email preview) which made users think the window was correctly aligned.
Hypothesis validated by creating tokens with explicit offset which succeed. Edge cases: some users on mobile mail clients where timezone metadata differs still see inconsistent behavior.
Potential fixes considered:
- Update email template to include ISO8601 timestamps with explicit timezone offset (preferred short-term).
- Harden token generation to always embed UTC timestamps and include timezone offset in the signed payload.
- Update RBAC token parser to accept naive timestamps assuming they are UTC rather than server-local (careful: backward-compat).
comments: 2026-03-11 09:15 - Maya Chen (Reporter): Noticed multiple EMEA engineers reporting they could not approve temporary access. Raised to SRE via #internal-support. Attached two example emails and one curl of the approval webhook.

2026-03-11 11:02 - Diego Ramos (Assignee): Able to reproduce in staging using locale override. I see rbac-service logs mark parsed_expiry_missing_tz. Adding more logging to approval-service to capture raw token payloads.

2026-03-11 13:45 - SRE Oncall (Anita Kapoor): Temporary mitigation: increased approval-service TTL from 10m to 45m for the next 2 hours to reduce immediate impact while we investigate. Noted this is a blunt instrument; revert after patch.

2026-03-12 08:30 - Diego Ramos: Created PR to change email template to include RFC3339 formatted expiry with 'Z' suffix (https://github.com/redwood-inference/approval-service/pull/4567). Also added extra assertion in rbac-service to log original token expiry string for future audits.
2026-03-13 10:22 - QA (Liam O'Neill): Verified canary deploy in us-east succeeded; approval flows with Europe/Berlin accounts now grant role as expected. Monitoring for 24 hours.
resolution: Workaround applied: temporary TTL increase and manual grants available via rbac-console. Permanent fix: merged PR to change email template to include explicit RFC3339 expiry offsets and a parser guard in rbac-service to accept RFC3339 with or without offset. Canary rollout completed in us-east; full rollout scheduled and completed 2026-03-13 10:00 UTC. Follow-up action: runbook updated to include test vector for non-US locales and add end-to-end tests for approval tokens in staging. Close after 24h stability window if no regressions.
